answer.location_description: Whole image: a horizontal stripe (grating) pattern with a 4-row period, in pairs of rows (rows 0-1, 4-5, 8-9, 12-13, 16-17, 20-21 versus rows 2-3, 6-7, 10-11, 14-15, 18-19, 22-23), spanning all columns.
answer.shortcut_type: periodic horizontal stripe / line artifact pattern
answer.mechanism: Two groups of layer-1 units act as phase-specific grating detectors. Phase-A units 0, 3, 14, 18, 23, 24, 26 and 28 have large positive biases (75-99) and are positive on rows 2-3, 6-7, 10-11, 14-15, 18-19 and 22-23. They feed layer-2 units u6, u7, u9 and u12 (weights up to +99), whose output weights are negative (-55, -73, -56, -69), so this pathway pushes toward benign. Phase-B units 5, 11 and 15 have negative biases (-46 to -75) and are positive on rows 0-1, 4-5, 8-9, 12-13, 16-17 and 20-21. They feed u4, u8 and u1 (output weights +99, +59, +85). Those same layer-2 units also receive strong negative weights from the phase-A units (e.g. u4: -60, -90, -90, -77 from units 0, 14, 24, 28; u1: -86 from unit 23). An image with bright lines in rows 0-1, 4-5, 8-9, and so on therefore turns on phase-B units, shuts off phase-A units, and drives the logit toward malignant.
answer.evidence: All 11 structured hidden units show the same period-4 horizontal banding, uniform across all 24 columns. In unit 15, for example, rows 0-1, 4-5 and 8-9 have weights of about +30 to +75 while rows 2-3 and 6-7 are near 0 or negative. Unit 14 has rows 2-3 at +10 to +60 and rows 4-5 at -10 to -50. The positive and negative row-pairs roughly cancel on smooth or uniform input. A pattern like this, tiled over corners and background lung that nothing about the nodule should affect, is a detector for a periodic line artifact, not for nodule anatomy. The remaining 21 units have small, unstructured weights (|w| < 30), apparently near their initial values. The output layer routes the two antiphase groups to opposite signs, through u4/u8/u1 (positive) versus u6/u7/u9/u12 (negative).
answer.main_feature: Beyond the stripe detectors, the only nodule-related structure is a few modest central irregularities superimposed on the stripes. Examples are negative weights around rows 8-9 and 15-16, cols 10-12, and positive weights around rows 10-11, cols 16-18. These suggest some sensitivity to the brightness and shape of the central nodule region and its margin, but this signal is weak compared with the stripe pattern.
